newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end mixed in thin, lackluster trade.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end mixed in thin, lackluster trade.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed mixed following a session of thin, lackluster trade as a key U.S. economic report failed to provide clear direction for the market, analysts said.

"Everybody is sort of mixed on the inflation outlook so it's just going back and forth here," said Hank Cunningham, a bond trader with First Marathon Securities. "The whole curve got a little bit steeper here."
Canada's 8.0 percent bond due 2023 fell C$0.15 to C$101.25 to yield 7.885 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark fell 1/32 to yield 7.11 percent.
The spread between benchmark bonds widened to 78 basis points from 76 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.

Canadian and U.S. bond traders had been eagerly awiting the release of the U.S. Federal Reserve's Beige Book at 1200 EDT/1600 GMT today for hints on the next move by the U.S. Federal Reserve. The report provides an anecdotal description of business and economic conditions.
In the report the Fed cited greater upward pressure on wages than prices, but called inflation signs "inconclusive." Bond prices seesawed but stayed negative following the report.

Investors are now looking ahead to the release of key U.S. producer price data on Thursday and Canadian and U.S. consumer price data on Friday for clues to the next moves by the Fed and Bank of Canada, analysts said.
In new issue news, the Bank of Montreal announced an issue of C$300 million of subordinated debentures due in October, 2006. The issue was well recieved by the market, Cunningham said.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 fell C$0.06 to C$97.01 to yield 7.421 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark traded unchanged to yield 6.93 percent.
The spread between the two bonds was 49 basis points, unchanged from the close of trading on Tuesday.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.85 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.30 percent.
